{{Quote|Freia lures the Neimoidians to Imynusoph, whose natives seem peaceable, ''[&hellip;]''|Excerpts from the program for the [[2 ABY/Legends|38:2:13]] premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
The '''Imynusoph system''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Star system/Legends|star system]] that contained the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Imynusoph/Legends|Imynusoph]]. Around [[3694 BBY]], the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] charted the [[Hydian Spur|final segment]] of the [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] that would become known as the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] to the system. Nearly four [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] after Kallea extended the Hydian Way to the Imynusoph system, the latter remained outside of the borders of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] governments but was considered part of the [[Kallea sector/Legends|Kallea sector]] by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].

According to the [[Opera/Legends|opera]] ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', Imynusoph was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Imyni/Legends|Imyni]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The [[Music/Legends|opera]] depicted the attempt by Kallea to capture her rivals [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]] in the [[Temple of Imynusoph]], with her plans waylaid by the betrayal of the Imyni and the arrival of reinforcements for both the scout's and the Osaaxes' side of the confrontation. In the opera's climax, a battle ensued between the parties present on Imynusoph.

==Description==
The Imynusoph system was located within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Kallea sector/Legends|Kallea sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It contained the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Imynusoph/Legends|Imynusoph]].<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
===Exploration===
In [[3694 BBY]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] extended a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] she had previously blazed that connected the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] with the [[Terminus system/Legends|Terminus system]]. Kallea charted a new route, which would eventually be named the [[Hydian Spur]], from [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]] to the Imynusoph [[Star system/Legends|system]]. The Hydian Spur went on to become the final segment of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] stretching across the entire [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="TEA" />

The area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] surrounding the Imynusoph system had been explored by [[3000 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Outer Rim system fell outside the borders of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> Shortly after the acquisition of the planet [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]] by the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] during that conflict, the Imynusoph system was featured on a [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Map/Legends|map]] displayed on a [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]] at a facility run by [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]], the [[Magistrate/Legends|Magistrate]]<ref name="AoI">''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]''</ref> of the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]].<ref name="DB Argente">{{DB|character|passelargente|Argente, Passel}}</ref> The system remained outside the sphere of influence of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]],<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> although it became incorporated as part of the Empire's Kallea [[Sector/Legends|sector]] by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].<ref name="EAOC" />

===''The Kallea Cycle''===
{{Quote|''[&hellip;]'' even as the Neimoidians summon a band of Gran and Dug thugs they've brought for protection&mdash;and Sival Brentioch ''[&hellip;]'' arrives with a fleet from Brentaal. In the battle that follows, Banu saves Freia but is mortally wounded.|Excerpts from the program for the [[2 ABY/Legends|38:2:13]] premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
Twenty-two [[Standard century/Legends|hundred]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after Kallea blazed the Hydian Way, the [[Musician/Legends|composer]] [[Trebian Shullos]] wrote ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', an [[Opera/Legends|opera]] that depicted how the resolute scout overcame the difficulties in charting the extensive hyperlane. The climax of the third and final act of the [[Music/Legends|opera]] took place on Imynusoph.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:The_Kallea_Cycle.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Imynusoph system was the setting of the climax in the opera ''The Kallea Cycle''.]]
In the opera, Kallea attempted to exact revenge on her rivals [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]] by setting a trap for them on Imynusoph. The Human scout lured the two [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] to a great [[Temple of Imynusoph|temple]] there. To the horror of the Osaaxes, Kallea revealed herself at a banquet at the temple and ordered the native [[Imyni/Legends|Imyni]] to bind the Neimoidians.<ref name="TEA" />

However, the natives chose that moment to turn on all the offworlders as a result of Kallea's high-handed attitude. At the same [[Time/Legends|time]], a band of [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] and [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Mercenary/Legends|thugs]] hired by the Neimoidians for protection arrived on Imynusoph, and so did a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] led by Kallea's secret admirer and patron, [[Sival Brentioch]].<ref name="TEA" />

During the climactic [[Battle on Imynusoph|battle]] that ensued, the temple was set [[Fire/Legends|ablaze]], and Kallea was saved by her fellow scout, the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Banu Hydia]], at the cost of his own life. In the opera's denouement, the Osaaxes were arrested, and Kallea and Brentioch left Imynusoph, taking Hydia's body with them for [[Burial/Legends|burial]] on their [[Homeworld/Legends|native world]], [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Freia orders the Imyni to bind the Neimoidians, but the Imyni turn on all the outworlders ''[&hellip;]''|Excerpts from the program for the 38:2:13 premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
Around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the Imynusoph system numbered less than one million. In the opera ''The Kallea Cycle'', Imynusoph was depicted as home to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] Imyni [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Imynusoph system was first mentioned in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid square J-21.<ref name="TEA" /> Fry has [[:File:JasonFryAtlas.png|stated]] that the star systems listed in ''The Essential Atlas''{{'s}} Appendix section are named after the most prominent planets or celestial bodies located in those systems. This article therefore considers the Imynusoph system to be named after the planet Imynusoph, which is assumed to have existed in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' galaxy independently of its [[in-universe]] depiction in ''The Kallea Cycle''.<ref name="Fry">{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/294887358405410816|[[Jason Fry]]|quote=Pretty much." and "planets not assigned a system in [a] published source can be assumed to reside in [the] system of [the] same name.}} {{C|In response to: "the systems in the Atlas's appendix are named after their most prominent planet/celestial body, correct?"}}</ref> ''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]'', a [[Star Wars comic books|webcomic]] authored by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="AoI" /> over the span of the 2009<ref name="AoI announcement">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20091001comics/index.html|text=New ''Clone Wars'' Web Comic Tells Original Tale}}</ref>&ndash;[[2010]]<ref name="Lethal Trackdown Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode222.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lethal Trackdown}}</ref> [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series,<ref name="AoI announcement" /> featured the first appearance of the Imynusoph system.<ref name="AoI" />
